title: Canals: an open-source Python workbench for open-channel hydraulic design
description:
Standalone Python 3 / PySide6 workbench for classical open-channel hydraulic design: optimal sections (Manning), hydraulic structures (gates, siphons, pressure breakers), regime earth-canal design (Lacey, Kennedy), gradually varied flow profiles, hydraulic jumps with USBR stilling-basin selection, and water-hammer screening. Ships a GUI, a JSON-emitting CLI, and an importable Python API under the MIT license.

v1.4.1 maintenance release. Corrects the Lacey velocity normalization (the 140 constant was applied twice), the regime-geometry root selection (analytic quadratic instead of a single-start fsolve, with an explicit infeasibility flag), and the Manning roughness handling in manning_design() (the passed n is used instead of a hardcoded 1/0.025). Implementations were verified against an independent 50-check campaign executed through both the Python API and the CLI; remaining limitations (Kennedy width bound on mild slopes, CLI water-hammer closure-time parity) are tracked as GitHub issues on the v1.4.1 milestone.
